Relatively spared. Encoding and free recall reduced in a dysexecutive (retrieval) pattern, but recognition and cued recall are comparatively preserved.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state the features present (disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, compulsive behaviour, dysexecutive profile), the functional decline, and the level of certainty (probable with frontal hypometabolism on functional imaging; definite if a pathogenic variant is found), and state that a near-normal MRI does not exclude bvFTD.

Explain why a primary psychiatric disorder does not account for the syndrome: no previous psychiatric illness, onset at 48, a progressive course with loss of insight, no depressive, manic or psychotic features, and no response to quetiapine; review the quetiapine with her psychiatrist, since it has brought no benefit and may raise glucose.
Address financial and legal capacity urgently: the real estate contracts, her role as a senior partner, power of attorney and protection of family assets; also address driving.
Arrange caregiver education and support for her husband and their teenage daughter.
Offer genetic counselling given onset at 48, before any genetic test and before any predictive testing of relatives.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET or perfusion SPECT is the functional study when one is needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, young-onset, previously misdiagnosed as a psychiatric disorder

differential.diagnosis: New-onset primary psychiatric disorder (late-onset bipolar disorder or schizophrenia)
differential.key_features: Against it: no previous psychiatric illness, no elevated mood, reduced sleep or psychosis, PHQ-9 4, progressive course with loss of insight, social-cognition impairment and frontal hypometabolism (Ducharme 2020).
Against it: preserved recognition memory and hippocampi, posterior metabolism preserved. An amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.
Against it: 20-month gradual course, no seizures or fluctuation, normal MRI signal and normal inflammatory markers.
The behavioural change began 17 months before quetiapine was started at 25 mg.

key_clinical_evidence: New disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy and compulsive rules over 20 months at age 48, with no psychiatric history, loss of insight and loss of her job; PHQ-9 4; MoCA 25/30.
Neuropsychology: executive and social-cognition impairment with relatively spared recognition memory and visuospatial function.
Near-normal MRI (borderline right frontal sulcal prominence) with bilateral frontal hypometabolism, right greater than left, on FDG-PET.
The behavioural change preceded quetiapine and did not respond to it.
Optional genetic work-up: low plasma progranulin and a pathogenic GRN nonsense variant, which make the diagnosis definite.

behavioural variant frontotemporal demen.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. New behavioural change in mid-life with progressive functional decline should prompt a neurodegenerative work-up even in a person with a psychiatric history. C9orf72 expansions and GRN and MAPT variants cause most familial FTD; counselling precedes any genetic test and any predictive testing of relatives. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. A is a 48-year-old senior partner at an accounting firm who is referred to the cognitive neurology clinic by her psychiatrist, who notes: 'I have been treating her for 5 months for presumed new-onset mood instability but I am concerned this is not a primary psychiatric condition.' Her husband of 22 years is the primary historian and describes a 20-month history of progressive changes that have been devastating to their family and her career. She has no prior psychiatric history. Approximately 20 months ago, her husband began noticing changes in her behavior at work events: she would make strikingly blunt and sometimes offensive comments about colleagues' appearance or personal choices, then appear confused by others' reactions. She began sending repetitive emails, exact duplicate messages to the same recipients, unaware that she had already sent them. Her work performance declined: she made a significant error on a large audit, which she denied for weeks despite clear documentation. She was placed on administrative leave 4 months ago following a formal complaint by a junior colleague about inappropriate behavior at a work event. She then signed multiple real estate purchase contracts in a 2-week period totaling approximately $850,000, a completely uncharacteristic impulse for a person her husband describes as 'the most financially conservative person I've ever known.' She proposed that the family move to three different cities simultaneously. She has become fixated on rearranging furniture in the house, doing so multiple times per week. She has developed what her husband calls 'rules' about household objects: their positions, colors, specific arrangements that must not be disturbed. She has completely stopped reading novels, a lifelong passion. She reacts with rage when a lunch order is wrong, and she propositioned one of her husband's colleagues at a business dinner. She shows no empathy for family members, including their teenage daughter who has been deeply distressed by the changes. The psychiatrist's diagnosis of 'mood instability' led to quetiapine 25 mg, which has had no effect on behaviors. She does not feel depressed and says she is only 'stressed'.

neurological_exam.additional: History from her husband. No primitive reflexes. No parkinsonism, fasciculations or apraxia.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and cooperative. Fluent speech. She feels she is 'stressed'; her husband states she is 'a completely different person.' When told she found a word-generation task hard she dismissed it as 'not a fair test.' No psychotic features. No pressured speech or elevated mood.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal strength and tone. No rigidity, no tremor.
